name: Empagliflozin
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Heart failure; CKD at risk of progression; cardiovascular risk in type 2 diabetes
usual_adult_dose.dose: 10 mg once daily in the morning
10 mg once daily; may increase to 25 mg (not recommended for glycemic control if eGFR <30)

key_interactions.effect: More urine volume and voiding; volume depletion risk.
key_interactions.action: Check volume status and kidney function before starting; monitor after.
Lower insulin or secretagogue doses may be needed.
Check lithium levels more often when starting or changing the dose.
Use other methods to monitor glycemic control.

common: Urinary tract infections and female genital mycotic infections (≥5%)
serious: Lower limb amputation (signal in some SGLT2 inhibitor studies)

contraindications: Hypersensitivity to empagliflozin or any excipient
monitoring: Kidney function before starting and as indicated
Withhold at least 3 days before surgery or prolonged fasting; watch for ketoacidosis
Genital and urinary infection symptoms; foot ulcers

pk.half_life_eskd: Not reported; AUC about 48% higher in patients on dialysis (label)
pk.metabolism: Glucuronidation (UGT2B7, UGT1A3, UGT1A8, UGT1A9); no major plasma metabolites
pk.excretion_renal_pct: 54.4% of radioactivity in urine (about half unchanged); 41.2% in feces
pk.dialyzability: Unknown: removal by hemodialysis not studied (label).
